inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares 480.0m, Q1 FY2027 10-Q EPS reconciliation (quarter ended 2026-08-30). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-count. No non-SBC issuance planned.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: stock-settled share-based payments expense 54.7 plus 19.8 'exercise of stock options and issuance of other stock awards, including tax withholdings' (financing; net outflow treated as equity-award tax). No combined adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation figure in the extracted filings, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.0 at ~4x net debt/EBITDA (asset beta of US packaged food ~0.5) gives cost of equity ~9.3%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.4% (Sep-2026 5.40% notes due 2031) = ~4.1% after tax; market weights ~50/50 (equity ~$7.3bn, net debt ~$7.4bn) -> ~6.7%, rounded up to 7.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged through the scenario paths and weights, not a stacked premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost sits inside cost of goods sold / SG&A, so it is already inside the EBITDA margin path; operating lease liabilities (~$207m at FY2026) are therefore NOT added to net debt. One treatment, applied once. lease_cost_pct_path is zero.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: US operating company, consumer staples manufacturer). First valuation of CAG, no prior DCF or memory entry. NORMALISATION: FY2026 statutory operating loss of -$1,628.4m is driven by $2,929.6m of non-cash goodwill ($2,382.4m, Refrigerated & Frozen) and brand ($547.2m) impairments plus a $42.2m divestiture gain; restating for those and restructuring 45.7, legal -37.4, CEO separation 8.1 and environmental 5.4 gives adjusted operating profit ~$1,281m (11.4% margin). Adding D&A 396.0, equity-method earnings 140.7 (+7.5 Ardent Mills restructuring) and SBC 54.7 gives a pre-SBC EBITDA of ~$1,880m = 16.7% of sales (FY2025 same basis ~19.5%, FY2024 ~21%). The EBITDA margin path is on that basis: it INCLUDES Ardent Mills equity earnings (44% JV, pass-through LLC taxed at Conagra level; FY2026 earnings 140.7 roughly equal to cash distributions), so no separate Ardent Mills asset is added in the equity bridge. FY2027 guidance (reaffirmed at Q1 FY2027, 30-Sep-2026): organic sales -1% to -3%, adjusted operating margin 10.0-10.5%, adjusted EPS $1.40-1.50, capex ~$550m, ~$250m debt paydown, leverage ~4x at year end. That maps to ~15.8% pre-SBC EBITDA and 5.0% capex in year 1. The impairments are treated as non-cash and non-recurring, but they are evidence: they record that the Pinnacle brands earn less than they were bought for, which is why the base margin path recovers only partway toward the FY2024-25 level. OWNER FCF: last_fcf = reported FCF 978.7 - SBC incl. equity-award taxes 74.5 - interest income 0 (net debt, no stripping) = 904.2. Reported FCF is post-interest (~$380m interest expense); the engine builds UNLEVERED flows from components and deducts net debt once. NET DEBT: Q1 FY2027 balance sheet (2026-08-30) notes payable 32.5 + current LTD 787.5 + senior LTD 6,940.1 = 7,760.1 less cash 371.6 = 7,388.5. The Metrics CSV TotalDebt of 8,517.5 for Q1 2027 does not tie to the face of the balance sheet and was not used. Pension/OPEB deficits are not deducted (not material to the extracted balance sheet; flag if a later filing shows a large unfunded position). BUYBACKS: $15.3m in FY2026 and $44m in Q1 FY2027 against $54.7m SBC -- the flat count is roughly funded; dividend cut 50% in July 2026 to $0.175/qtr with freed cash going to debt paydown. HORIZON: 10 years, because capex steps down from the 5.0% guided peak and margins recover through ~year 5.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-10.3% 3yr, -5.9% 5yr) is driven by $2.93bn of FY2026 non-cash impairments and is not a usable growth proxy; EPS CAGRs are undefined because FY2026 diluted EPS is -$4.00 (FY2021 $2.67 -> FY2025 $2.41 is -2.5%/yr on the last clean pair). Revenue 5yr CAGR (+0.2%) selected; organic volumes have declined six straight years and FY2027 guides organic -1% to -3%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (equity-award taxes not available for the full history, so the CAGR series uses SBC only). Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR of 18.6% is a base effect from a depressed FY2023 (633 reported, inventory build and cost inflation) and is not a forward signal; the 5yr owner-FCF CAGR is 0.6%. SBC is ~0.5% of sales, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs move together -- no stock-paid growth issue here.

base.narrative: FY2027 lands inside guidance (sales ~-2%, adjusted operating margin ~10.3%); the frozen price-for-margin reset and Project Catalyst productivity recover about one point of EBITDA margin by FY2031, still ~2.7pp below FY2025 and ~4pp below FY2024. Volumes stabilise and nominal growth settles at ~1.5% from pricing. Capex steps down from the guided ~$550m peak to the historical ~3.7% of sales.

bull.narrative: Brase's reset works: SKU simplification and less-elastic frozen pricing arrest the volume slide by FY2028, GLP-1 adoption proves a net tailwind for portion-controlled frozen meals and meat snacks/popcorn, and Foodservice keeps compounding. Margin recovers to ~18.2% (between FY2025 and FY2024 levels) as Catalyst savings stick and Ardent Mills normalises; leverage reaches ~3x and capex falls back to 3.5%.

bear.narrative: Volume erosion continues: price increases in H2 FY2027 meet elasticity above historical levels, private label takes more of shelf-stable staples, Walmart (~29% of sales) presses terms, and GLP-1 turns into a net headwind for snacks. Revenue falls ~11% over five years and EBITDA margin compresses toward 14% as fixed plant costs deleverage; further divestitures at low multiples shrink the base. Leverage stays ~4x, constraining reinvestment.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 inside guidance (organic sales ~-2%, adjusted operating margin ~10.3%); partial margin recovery of ~1pp by FY2031 from frozen price discipline and Project Catalyst; volumes stabilise and growth settles at ~1.5% nominal; capex normalises from a 5% peak to 3.7%. Value roughly equals today's enterprise value: the market is pricing the reset, not a recovery.
scenario_narratives.bull: The reset arrests six years of volume decline by FY2028; GLP-1 lifts portion-controlled frozen meals and protein snacks; Foodservice grows; margin rebuilds to ~18% (still below FY2024's ~21%), leverage reaches the 3x target and the equity re-rates as debt falls.
scenario_narratives.bear: Elasticity stays above historical norms, private label and Walmart squeeze staples, GLP-1 is a net headwind for snacks, and revenue shrinks ~11% over five years with margin sliding to ~14%. Leverage stays near 4x; with 4x leverage, a modest enterprise-value miss is a large equity miss.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: six consecutive years of organic volume decline, FY2027 guidance itself embedding further decline, net leverage ~4x (equity is a thin slice of EV so EV misses are magnified), 29% Walmart concentration, and a first-time CEO executing an unproven reset. Base 50%: guidance was reaffirmed and Q1 FY2027 beat. Bull cut to 20% because it needs volume stabilisation, a GLP-1 tailwind and margin recovery to all go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Conagra is a mature, ex-growth US packaged-food manufacturer carrying ~4x leverage. The FY2026 loss is non-cash impairment, not cash collapse -- normalised EBITDA was ~$1.9bn and owner FCF ~$0.9bn -- but the impairments confirm a lower earning power than the Pinnacle-era base. The valuation therefore normalises earnings to guidance rather than to FY2024-25 margins, caps the terminal at 10-14x FCF with 0-1.5% growth, and weights the bear case at 30% because leverage turns modest operating misses into large equity misses.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: ~$7.4bn net debt against ~$7.3bn of equity value; every 1x of EV/EBITDA is ~$3.9/share
Volume elasticity on the H2 FY2027 price increases (management says elasticity is running above historical levels)
Walmart concentration (~29% of sales) and private-label share gains in shelf-stable staples
GLP-1 adoption: assumed roughly neutral in base; a net snack headwind is a bear-case driver
Further impairments signal the brand base; Refrigerated & Frozen has no remaining fair-value cushion
Ardent Mills earnings (~$140-180m) are commodity-sensitive and inside the EBITDA path
